project.name: bioFM
project.description:
The code half of the bioFM workspace: two independent Python packages. `chipsim` is an in-silico lung-on-a-chip exposure and barrier-response pipeline (ingest → harmonize → encoders → heads → transport → occupancy → surface → uncertainty → eval → acquire) built on RDKit, pandas and DVC, with a record-content guard and a `chipsim` CLI. `perturb-eval` is an agentic evaluation harness that pits contextual Bayesian optimization against evolutionary hyperparameter tuning on perturb-seq mean-squared-difference benchmarks, with a Modal-based remote execution layer. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

Known limitation: the import graph is incomplete. An independent AST pass over all 277 scanned files found 235 real internal Python import pairs; only 100 are represented as edges here. The 135 absent ones fall to two extractor gaps — imports written inside function bodies are not collected (every Modal remote-function import, and lazy imports in Typer subcommands), and a Poetry src-layout package cannot be resolved from a sibling directory such as scripts/ or tests/. The absence of an `imports` edge therefore means "the resolver could not see it", NEVER "no relationship exists". Do not read low fan-in as dead code: perturb_eval's entire driver layer under scripts/ is affected.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the end-to-end agentic perturb-seq lifecycle; re-exports the four executed-step DTOs so callers never reach into the private modules.

nodes.name: architect_dispatch.py
nodes.summary: Translates the Architect agent's free-form proposed configuration into a concrete BackbonePredictor plus a normalised training config, applying the round's critique delta.

nodes.name: resolve_architect_config
nodes.summary: Normalises an Architect proposal (backbone name, HVG count, learning rate, epochs) into a validated config dict, folding in the previous round's critique delta and falling back to safe defaults.

nodes.name: dispatch_architect
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that resolves an Architect proposal and instantiates the matching backbone predictor in one call.

nodes.name: data_curator_exec.py
nodes.summary: Executes the DataCurator agent's QC recipe against the expression matrix, materialising the agent-chosen HVG selection so the downstream Trainer and Validator see exactly what was proposed.

nodes.name: execute_data_curator
nodes.summary: Applies the proposed number of highly-variable genes (and logs the mito-% threshold) to the count matrix, returning the curated matrix plus the retained gene indices.

nodes.name: literature_exec.py
nodes.summary: Minimal Literature agent executor that pulls the expected perturbation-response genes out of the agent's proposal payload.

nodes.name: extract_expected_genes
nodes.summary: Extracts the list of genes the Literature agent expects to respond to the perturbation from its proposal dict.

nodes.name: loop.py
nodes.summary: The multi-round agentic lifecycle driver: propose to execute to critique to refine, threading the Validator's rationale and previous MSD into the next round's context and stopping early once the Validator accepts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a typing.Protocol (AgentPool) so the production CellForge pool and the offline MockAgentPool are interchangeable without inheritance.

nodes.name: run_agentic_lifecycle
nodes.summary: Runs up to max_rounds of the five-agent propose/execute/critique cycle over a real expression matrix, recording every step and terminating early when the Validator gate accepts.

nodes.name: AgentPool
nodes.summary: Structural Protocol describing the single method (propose) the lifecycle loop needs from any agent pool implementation.

nodes.name: MockAgentPool
nodes.summary: Deterministic, seeded stand-in for the production CellForge agent pool so the lifecycle loop stays testable offline.

nodes.name: trainer_exec.py
nodes.summary: Executes the Trainer agent's recipe by fitting the chosen backbone on the curated matrix and timing the fit.

nodes.name: execute_trainer
nodes.summary: Builds a BackboneTrainConfig from the Trainer proposal, fits the backbone on the control/perturbed split, and returns the fit artifacts with wall time.

nodes.name: types.py
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass DTOs carrying one executed agent step, one validation verdict, and the full lifecycle run record.
nodes.languageNotes: All carriers are frozen dataclasses so a logged lifecycle run can be hashed and serialised without defensive copies.

nodes.name: ExecutedProposal
nodes.summary: One agent's proposal after it was actually executed: content, rationale, LLM confidence, artifact path, wall time and success flag.

nodes.name: StructuredCritiqueDTO
nodes.summary: Machine-readable Validator critique naming which genes failed, the suggested next-round config delta, and the accept reason.

nodes.name: ExecutedValidation
nodes.summary: Validator verdict for a round: MSD on top-K genes, BioFM agreement, DEG overlap, accept flag and the attached structured critique.

nodes.name: LifecycleStep
nodes.summary: Per-round, per-agent record appended to the lifecycle run log.

nodes.name: LifecycleRun
nodes.summary: Terminal record for one lifecycle: every step plus final MSD, validator agreement, round/agent counts and the backbone used.

nodes.name: validator_gate.py
nodes.summary: The Validator agent step: scores a trained backbone on held-out perturbations, gates acceptance on MSD, and emits a structured critique the next round's Architect can consume.

nodes.name: suggest_config_delta
nodes.summary: Derives the next-round config delta from the current verdict, rotating the backbone through linear -> mlp -> scgpt_small when MSD misses the threshold.

nodes.name: score_and_gate
nodes.summary: Predicts held-out log fold-changes, computes MSD on the top-K differentially expressed genes plus sign agreement, and returns an accept/reject verdict with a structured critique.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Backbone-predictor registry: maps the names linear, mlp and scgpt_small to their classes and re-exports the shared protocol, config and metric helpers.

nodes.name: available_backbones
nodes.summary: Returns the registered backbone names, omitting scgpt_small when PyTorch is not installed.

nodes.name: build_backbone
nodes.summary: Instantiates a backbone predictor by registry name, raising on an unknown or unavailable name rather than falling back silently.

nodes.name: base.py
nodes.summary: Shared contract for the backbone predictors: the BackbonePredictor Protocol plus the pure NumPy helpers (MSD, per-perturbation mean, log fold-change) every experiment runner depends on.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses typing.Protocol rather than an ABC so experiment runners depend on the structural contract, not on any concrete backbone.

nodes.name: BackboneTrainConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen knob set passed to every backbone fit call: top-K genes, seed, max iterations, learning rate and ridge penalty.

nodes.name: BackboneFitArtifacts
nodes.summary: Frozen record returned by a fit: backbone name, number of training perturbations, train seconds and a free-form extra dict.

nodes.name: BackbonePredictor
nodes.summary: Structural Protocol every concrete backbone must satisfy: a name, a fit and a predict_logfc.

nodes.name: mean_squared_deviation
nodes.summary: Computes mean squared deviation between predicted and observed log fold-changes restricted to the top-K gene indices.

nodes.name: per_perturbation_mean
nodes.summary: Averages the expression matrix rows within each perturbation label, returning a label-to-mean-vector mapping.

nodes.name: log_fold_change
nodes.summary: Computes the log fold-change of a perturbed mean against the control mean with a pseudocount guard against log(0).

nodes.name: linear.py
nodes.summary: Ridge-regularised linear backbone: the cheapest predictor in the registry and the baseline every other backbone is scored against.

nodes.name: LinearBackbone
nodes.summary: Closed-form ridge regression from perturbation one-hot features to per-gene log fold-change; fits in milliseconds and serves as the grid's baseline.

nodes.name: mlp.py
nodes.summary: Small NumPy multilayer-perceptron backbone sitting between the linear baseline and the transformer in capacity.

nodes.name: MLPBackbone
nodes.summary: Two-layer perceptron trained by minibatch gradient descent on featurised perturbation inputs, predicting per-gene log fold-change.

nodes.name: scgpt_small.py
nodes.summary: From-scratch ~2.1M-parameter scGPT-like transformer backbone with rank-value gene binning and a LoRA perturbation head; imports cleanly without PyTorch as long as it is not instantiated.
nodes.languageNotes: PyTorch is probed via importlib.util.find_spec so the module stays importable in torch-free environments — instantiating the class is what raises.

nodes.name: _ArchitectureConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen hyperparameter record for the small transformer: bins, embedding dim, layers, heads, FFN width, gene vocab and LoRA rank.

nodes.name: SCGPTSmallBackbone
nodes.summary: Gene-as-token transformer backbone: masked-expression pretraining on control cells followed by LoRA finetuning of a perturbation head, padded back to the full gene space for prediction.

nodes.name: drugbank_snapshot.py
nodes.summary: Fetches, hash-verifies and parses the pinned public DrugBank 4.2 snapshot (dhimmel/drugbank), taking only compound identity and drug-to-transporter edges — never affinities, and never redistributing the source data.
nodes.languageNotes: Downloads land under a git-ignored, DVC-tracked data/raw/ tree and every artifact carries a SHA-256 digest sidecar, so the snapshot is reproducible without being vendored.

nodes.name: SnapshotFetchError
nodes.summary: Raised when the pinned snapshot cannot be fetched or its hash does not match the manifest.

nodes.name: _validate_commit
nodes.summary: Rejects anything that is not a 40-character hex commit before it is interpolated into a download URL.

nodes.name: fetch_snapshot
nodes.summary: Downloads each pinned snapshot file to the git-ignored raw data directory and returns the SHA-256 digest of every file it wrote.

nodes.name: verify_snapshot
nodes.summary: Re-hashes the downloaded snapshot files and compares them against the manifest, failing loudly on any mismatch or missing file.

nodes.name: vendored_offenders
nodes.summary: Lists any tracked path that would amount to redistributing DrugBank, the check that keeps the no-vendoring rule falsifiable.

nodes.name: load_compounds
nodes.summary: Parses the compound TSV into a frame, splitting pipe-joined list cells into real lists, dropping structureless rows and enforcing a row-count floor.

nodes.name: load_protein_edges
nodes.summary: Parses drug-to-protein edges, filters to human, and enforces category-set equality plus a row-count floor so organism drift raises rather than yielding a quietly empty frame.

nodes.name: write_compounds
nodes.summary: Writes the canonicalized compound frame to Parquet in a declared column order sorted by canonical key, refusing a frame that lacks canonical identity.

nodes.name: write_digest_sidecar
nodes.summary: Writes the git-trackable SHA-256 digest sidecar next to a Parquet artifact so byte-level drift is visible in review.

nodes.name: read_digest_sidecar
nodes.summary: Reads a digest sidecar back and returns the recorded hash for comparison against the artifact on disk.

nodes.name: _main
nodes.summary: Standalone argparse entry point for running fetch, verify and parse of the snapshot outside the main pipeline CLI.

nodes.name: test_adjudication.py
nodes.summary: Tests for the roster validator, the non-clobbering adjudication worksheet and the provenance display block — S11a, T13, T15 and T17 done-conditions.

nodes.name: test_t13_never_clobbers_a_partially_filled_worksheet
nodes.summary: Proves that regenerating the worksheet over a partially filled one preserves every human verdict — the module's central silent-failure guard.

nodes.name: test_t13_preserves_a_row_whose_only_human_content_is_a_doi
nodes.summary: Checks that a row whose sole human content is an evidence DOI still counts as human content and survives the merge.

nodes.name: test_parse.py
nodes.summary: Tests for snapshot parsing and compound-identity canonicalization — T5, T5a, T5b and T6 done-conditions including golden canonical keys and salt collapsing.

nodes.name: test_t6_raises_when_a_category_is_lost_to_the_organism_filter
nodes.summary: Proves that the human-organism filter raises when it would drop an entire edge category, rather than quietly shrinking the frame.

nodes.name: test_pgp_label.py
nodes.summary: Tests for the barrier-panel join, the three-way P-gp label and the panel seal — T9, T10 and T7a done-conditions, including that the label is never satisfied by a constant implementation.

nodes.name: test_fixture_face_agreement_with_live_panel
nodes.summary: Cross-checks that the test fixture's panel faces still agree with the live ratified panel, so fixture drift is caught rather than masked.

nodes.name: test_t7a_a_fixture_seal_is_not_valid_for_the_live_panel
nodes.summary: Proves a seal computed over the fixture panel does not validate the live panel, so the digest genuinely binds content.

nodes.name: test_t7a_seal_refuses_to_report_success_on_a_write_that_did_not_land
nodes.summary: Proves that a failed write during sealing surfaces as an error rather than a reported success.

nodes.name: test_provenance.py
nodes.summary: Tests for the nine-key provenance contract, snapshot hash agreement, the no-vendoring rule, the DVC pointer and the model card's ratification wording.

nodes.name: test_card_never_claims_the_seal_proves_authorship
nodes.summary: Pins the model card's wording so the panel seal is never described as proving who ratified the panel, only that its content is unchanged.

nodes.name: test_omitting_the_panel_renders_a_visible_gap_not_a_silent_one
nodes.summary: Proves that an absent panel produces a visible gap in the rendered card rather than a silently omitted section.

nodes.name: test_dvc_pointer_is_tracked
nodes.summary: Checks that the DVC pointer file for the raw snapshot is tracked in git while the payload itself is not.

nodes.name: test_a_malformed_seal_is_named_malformed_not_dressed_as_a_digest
nodes.summary: Proves a malformed seal value is reported as malformed rather than rendered as if it were a valid digest.

nodes.name: test_replay_determinism.py
nodes.summary: Replay-determinism control: proves the same config and seed reproduce byte-identical output, that the control can actually fail, and that determinism holds across separate processes.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes a deliberate negative control — the determinism assertion is exercised against a perturbed run to show it is falsifiable rather than vacuous.

nodes.name: test_determinism_holds_across_processes_not_just_within_one
nodes.summary: Runs the pipeline in a separate subprocess and compares artifacts byte for byte, ruling out within-process caching as the source of the agreement.

nodes.name: test_same_config_and_seed_reproduce_byte_identical_output
nodes.summary: The primary replay control: two runs from the same config and seed must produce byte-identical artifacts.

nodes.name: provenance_block.py
nodes.summary: Renders the model card's data-provenance block and panel-ratification section, composing the source-version string from the pinned snapshot fields rather than hard-coding it.
nodes.languageNotes: The version string is composed from upstream_version + snapshot_date by design — a hard-coded string would keep rendering a stale, confident falsehood after the snapshot is re-pinned.

nodes.name: format_source_version
nodes.summary: Composes the human-readable source-version string from the upstream version and snapshot date so it can never drift from the pinned provenance.

nodes.name: label_counts
nodes.summary: Tallies the three-way P-gp label series into yes/no/unknown counts, refusing nulls and out-of-domain values rather than silently bucketing them.

nodes.name: pgp_groups_usable
nodes.summary: Decides whether the label counts leave every P-gp group populated enough for the panel to be usable downstream.

nodes.name: render_data_provenance
nodes.summary: Builds the full data-provenance block: checks the provenance contract, renders the composed version string, the label counts, group usability and the commit-substitution rationale.

nodes.name: render_panel_ratification
nodes.summary: Renders the barrier-panel ratification section, naming a malformed or absent seal explicitly instead of dressing it up as a valid digest or leaving a silent gap.

nodes.name: adjudication.py
nodes.summary: P-gp adjudication worksheet writer and loader: merges without ever clobbering a human's verdict, and keeps 'unadjudicated' (empty) distinct from 'adjudicated as unknown'.
nodes.languageNotes: Two silent-failure modes shape the module: a routine ETL re-run must not blank hand-entered verdicts, and a blank worksheet must never read as a completed all-unknown one.

nodes.name: AdjudicationError
nodes.summary: Raised when a worksheet is incomplete, self-contradictory, or would lose a previously adjudicated verdict.

nodes.name: _has_any_human_content
nodes.summary: Detects whether a worksheet row carries any human-entered content, the test that decides whether a merge may overwrite it.

nodes.name: _read_worksheet
nodes.summary: Reads an existing adjudication worksheet from disk, rejecting duplicate canonical keys on the way in.

nodes.name: write_adjudication_worksheet
nodes.summary: Writes one worksheet row per roster entry with empty verdict columns, atomically merging over any existing file so every non-empty human verdict and added column survives.

nodes.name: adjudicate_pgp_labels
nodes.summary: Turns a fully filled worksheet into the per-compound three-way P-gp label series, raising on blanks, missing DOIs, missing adjudicators, duplicates and out-of-domain values.

nodes.name: read_pgp_labels
nodes.summary: Loads the adjudicated P-gp label series back from its Parquet artifact, preserving index metadata without renormalisation.

nodes.name: contracts.py
nodes.summary: The ratified nine-key provenance contract: nine keys present, eight always non-empty, and commit_change_rationale non-empty if and only if the audited commit differs from the source commit.
nodes.languageNotes: A conditional-presence contract, which is strictly more checkable than 'all keys non-empty' — a rationale offered for an unchanged commit is as much a violation as one missing for a changed commit.

nodes.name: ProvenanceContractError
nodes.summary: Raised when the provenance file violates the ratified nine-key contract.

nodes.name: load_provenance
nodes.summary: Reads the provenance YAML from disk into a plain dict for contract checking.

nodes.name: check_provenance
nodes.summary: Enforces the nine-key contract: key presence, non-emptiness of the eight unconditional keys, a 40-hex commit, and a correctly sized attribution list.

nodes.name: check_commit_substitution
nodes.summary: Enforces the biconditional rationale rule — a commit substitution must be justified, and an unchanged commit must carry no rationale.

nodes.name: ids.py
nodes.summary: Compound-identity canonicalization layer: RDKit salt stripping, neutralization and tautomer canonicalization to a canonical InChIKey, so a salt and its free base never split into two compounds.
nodes.languageNotes: Joining on raw InChIKey silently halves apparent label counts — verapamil and verapamil hydrochloride carry different raw keys but are the same compound downstream.

nodes.name: CanonicalizationError
nodes.summary: Raised when a structure cannot be parsed or canonicalized, rather than letting a null key through.

nodes.name: canonical_inchikey
nodes.summary: Canonicalizes one structure through RDKit uncharging, salt stripping and tautomer enumeration into a deterministic InChIKey, raising on unparseable or empty input.

nodes.name: add_canonical_identity
nodes.summary: Adds the canonical_inchikey column to a compound frame, guaranteeing a non-null key on every retained row.

nodes.name: canonicalization_disagreements
nodes.summary: Counts rows whose canonical key differs from the raw InChIKey — the observable measure of how much salt/tautomer collapsing actually happened.

nodes.name: pgp_label.py
nodes.summary: Barrier-panel join and the three-way P-gp substrate label, plus the panel seal: an unratified or unsealed panel raises, and absence of an ABCB1 edge yields 'unknown', never 'no'.
nodes.languageNotes: Two fail-loud invariants: a missing 'ratified' key is treated exactly like ratified:false, and 'no' is a positive claim assignable only by human adjudication with a citation.

nodes.name: panel_digest
nodes.summary: Computes the order-independent SHA-256 digest over the panel's substantive fields, the value the seal binds and every later load re-checks.

nodes.name: seal_panel
nodes.summary: Seals a ratified panel by writing its digest back into the file, refusing an unratified panel or one without a named ratifier and refusing to report success on a write that did not land.

nodes.name: load_ratified_panel
nodes.summary: Loads the barrier panel only when it is ratified, sealed and digest-consistent, raising on a missing ratified key, a missing or edited face, a duplicate symbol, or a broken seal.

nodes.name: barrier_panel_edges
nodes.summary: Joins the drug-to-protein edge frame onto the ratified panel accessions, dropping every off-panel accession.

nodes.name: resolve_panel_accession
nodes.summary: Resolves a gene symbol such as ABCB1 to its accession from the ratified panel, never from a hard-coded constant.

nodes.name: pgp_substrate_label
nodes.summary: Derives the three-way P-gp substrate label per canonical compound from ABCB1 transporter edges, emitting 'unknown' where there is no evidence and never inferring a negative.

nodes.name: roster.py
nodes.summary: Validates the human-written proof-of-concept compound roster — entry count, non-empty names, evidence DOIs, canonical keys and resolvability against the snapshot. It never generates a roster.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately validation-only: which compounds are 'lung-relevant with published exposure' is a human claim, so an auto-filter of the snapshot would not be a substitute.

nodes.name: RosterValidationError
nodes.summary: Raised when the hand-written roster is malformed, the wrong size, or names a key absent from the snapshot.

nodes.name: load_poc_roster
nodes.summary: Parses the roster YAML and validates every entry against the compound snapshot, stripping whitespace from keys and rejecting duplicates, blanks and unresolvable keys.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Barrel for the experiment runners; v0.5.0 dropped the synthetic-DGP runners so only the real Adamson/Norman entry-points are re-exported.

nodes.name: common.py
nodes.summary: Shared result carriers for the E2 grid and E3 optimizer experiments, plus the bridge that turns a RunTrace into a probe signature.

nodes.name: GridCellResult
nodes.summary: Frozen record for one (phi, task, seed) grid cell: the config id, task, seed, held-out MSD, wall time and backbone used.

nodes.name: OptimizerTrajectory
nodes.summary: Frozen trajectory for one optimizer: best-MSD-per-iteration, cumulative regret and the per-seed curves behind the averaged line.

nodes.name: probe_signature_from_trace
nodes.summary: Derives the four-dimensional probe signature (normalised ACE, mean and max confidence, critique dispersion) from a recorded RunTrace.

nodes.name: e2_adamson.py
nodes.summary: Real-data E2 trainer for Adamson 2016: reads the pilot .h5ad directly with h5py, normalises and log1p-transforms counts, applies a leave-one-perturbation-out split, and scores held-out MSD on top-K DEGs.
nodes.languageNotes: Reads AnnData HDF5 by hand with h5py and reconstructs CSR/CSC blocks rather than depending on scanpy, keeping the runner importable in slim environments.

nodes.name: load_adamson_combined
nodes.summary: Loads and concatenates several Adamson .h5ad files onto their shared gene intersection, re-selecting highly-variable genes across the pooled matrix.

nodes.name: load_adamson_matrix
nodes.summary: Reads one Adamson .h5ad via h5py, densifies the sparse expression block, log1p-normalises, selects HVGs, caps cells per perturbation and builds the control mask and target-gene index.

nodes.name: train_grid_cell_adamson
nodes.summary: Trains one grid cell end to end: loads (or reuses a cached) Adamson matrix, holds out one perturbation, fits the configured backbone and returns the held-out MSD as a GridCellResult.

nodes.name: e2_grid_fill.py
nodes.summary: E2 offline grid fill over (phi, task, seed): enumerates the configuration grid and persists the resulting MSD cells to JSONL when Parquet is unavailable.

nodes.name: enumerate_grid
nodes.summary: Produces the Cartesian product of configurations, tasks and seeds that the E2 grid must cover.

nodes.name: write_results_jsonl
nodes.summary: Appends grid-cell results to a JSONL cache, the Parquet-free fallback path for the E2 grid.

nodes.name: e3_optimizer_comparison.py
nodes.summary: E3 runner: replays each optimizer against an already-filled (phi, task) MSD grid for a fixed iteration budget, averaging across seeds and tasks to produce the supplement's headline iteration-vs-best-MSD figure.

nodes.name: run_e3_optimizer_comparison
nodes.summary: Runs every named optimizer against the cached MSD grid, feeding back observations each iteration and returning one OptimizerTrajectory per optimizer.

nodes.name: _collect_per_seed_trajectories
nodes.summary: Reruns an optimizer once per seed and task to build the per-seed best-so-far curves that back the averaged trajectory's error band.

nodes.name: instrumentation.py
nodes.summary: Non-invasive bridge from the CellForge orchestrator's ConsensusResult to this package's RunTrace, translating rounds, proposals and critiques without patching the orchestrator.
nodes.languageNotes: Duck-types the orchestrator result (anything with .rounds exposing .proposals and .critiques) so the evaluation layer stays swappable.

nodes.name: _build_critique_matrix
nodes.summary: Builds the N x (N-1) critique-severity matrix in agent-name order, so severity lookups are positional rather than name-keyed downstream.

nodes.name: round_trace_from_consensus_round
nodes.summary: Converts one orchestrator consensus round into a frozen RoundTrace: agent names, confidences, critique severities, winner index and consensus score.

nodes.name: run_trace_from_consensus
nodes.summary: Converts a full orchestrator ConsensusResult into a RunTrace, attaching the task id, backbone name and per-round compute tokens.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Optimizer registry: dispatches the names random, cma_es and contextual_gp to their implementations and re-exports the shared Observation carrier.

nodes.name: available_optimizers
nodes.summary: Returns the registered optimizer names.

nodes.name: build_optimizer
nodes.summary: Instantiates an optimizer by registry name over the given config space and seed, raising on an unknown name.

nodes.name: base.py
nodes.summary: Shared contract for the optimizer stack: the Optimizer Protocol, the Observation carrier and the embedding that maps a Config to and from its continuous vector relaxation.

nodes.name: Observation
nodes.summary: Frozen triple of the configuration tried, the context it was tried in, and the objective value observed.

nodes.name: Optimizer
nodes.summary: Structural Protocol every optimizer satisfies: a name and a suggest that maps past observations plus a context to the next Config.

nodes.name: config_to_vec
nodes.summary: Embeds a Config into the continuous vector the evolutionary and GP optimizers search over.

nodes.name: nearest_config
nodes.summary: Projects a continuous search vector back onto the nearest admissible Config in the discrete config space.

nodes.name: cma_es.py
nodes.summary: Dependency-free (1+lambda) evolution strategy over the continuous relaxation of the config space, adapting step size by Rechenberg's one-fifth success rule.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately a stripped-down ES rather than full CMA-ES so the core test suite stays NumPy-only; the real cma package sits in an optional dependency group.

nodes.name: OnePlusLambdaES
nodes.summary: Keeps a Gaussian search distribution (mean and scalar sigma), samples lambda offspring per suggest call, and adapts sigma from the observed success rate.

nodes.name: contextual_gp.py
nodes.summary: Contextual GP bandit with a factored Matern-5/2 times Hamming kernel — the supplement's primary methodological contribution, implemented in pure NumPy with an exact O(n^3) posterior.
nodes.languageNotes: Exact Gaussian posterior with no botorch or scikit-optimize dependency; acceptable because the target regime is under about 100 observations.

nodes.name: ContextualGPOptimizer
nodes.summary: Fits an exact GP over (config, context) pairs with the factored kernel and suggests the config maximising the acquisition at the queried context.

nodes.name: random_baseline.py
nodes.summary: Uniform random-search optimizer — the control every other optimizer's regret curve is measured against.

nodes.name: RandomOptimizer
nodes.summary: Ignores past observations and draws a uniformly random Config from the space on every suggest call.

nodes.name: types.py
nodes.summary: Immutable data carriers shared across the package: per-round and per-run orchestration traces, their derived metric records, and the Config that defines the HPO search axes.
nodes.languageNotes: Every carrier is frozen=True so a logged trace can be hashed and passed between processes without defensive copies.

nodes.name: RoundTrace
nodes.summary: One round of the five-agent orchestration: agent names, confidences, the critique-severity matrix, winner index, consensus score and compute tokens.

nodes.name: RunTrace
nodes.summary: A full orchestration run: the ordered RoundTraces plus task id, convergence flag and backbone, with derived round/agent counts.

nodes.name: RoundMetrics
nodes.summary: Metrics derived from one RoundTrace: ACE and its normalised form, confidence statistics, critique-severity dispersion and consensus score.

nodes.name: RunMetrics
nodes.summary: Run-level metrics: the per-round records plus delta-ACE, delta mean confidence, winner flip rate, final consensus score and TDI.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: The HPO configuration axes (agent count, round count, backbone) with the FLOPs proxy the budget constraint is expressed in.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Public surface of the perturb_eval package: re-exports the Bayesian recommender, the orchestration metrics, the preflight probe and the core trace types.
nodes.languageNotes: A Python package barrel — the __all__ list is the package's declared public API.

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: Module entry point so the package can be run as `python -m perturb_eval`, delegating straight to the Typer CLI app.

nodes.name: bayesian.py
nodes.summary: Bayesian recommender mapping a probe signature to the MAP configuration under a FLOPs budget, using a per-config Gaussian likelihood and a configurable size-favouring prior computed in log space.
nodes.languageNotes: Posterior is accumulated in log space with a diagonal covariance — deliberately simple because the calibration set is at most ~100 tasks over 4-d signatures.

nodes.name: Recommendation
nodes.summary: Frozen result of a recommendation: the chosen Config, its log posterior, the per-config log likelihoods, the full ranking, the budget applied and how many tasks the model was fit on.

nodes.name: BayesianRecommender
nodes.summary: Fits per-configuration Gaussian means and variances from labelled probe signatures, then returns the budget-feasible config maximising log prior plus log likelihood.

nodes.name: calibration.py
nodes.summary: Fits the TDI coefficients from logged runs with a small ridge regression, the calibration step that turns raw orchestration metrics into a single difficulty index.
nodes.languageNotes: Ridge rather than OLS specifically because the calibration set is small — the penalty keeps the four coefficients from blowing up on N of order tens.

nodes.name: TDICoeffs
nodes.summary: Frozen four-coefficient carrier (alpha, beta, gamma, delta) weighting the TDI terms, with a dict view for serialisation.

nodes.name: fit_tdi_coefficients
nodes.summary: Builds the design matrix from labelled RunTraces (delta-ACE, delta mean confidence, winner flip rate) and solves the ridge normal equations for the TDI coefficients.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: Typer command-line interface exposing `perturb-eval preflight | calibrate | evaluate` over the probe and recommender.

nodes.name: cmd_preflight
nodes.summary: Preflight command: assembles a ProbeSignature from the four scalar options, asks the recommender for a config under the budget, and echoes the result as JSON.

nodes.name: cmd_evaluate
nodes.summary: Evaluate command placeholder that raises NotImplementedError rather than silently returning a wrong result for a trace JSON.

nodes.name: massgen_adapter.py
nodes.summary: Exposes the evaluation pipeline as a MassGen skill: dict-in/dict-out preflight and evaluate entry points that never import MassGen itself, so the module stays importable without its dev dependencies.

nodes.name: preflight_skill
nodes.summary: MassGen preflight entry point: reads the probe scalars and budget out of a payload dict, runs the Bayesian recommender and returns a JSON-serialisable recommendation.

nodes.name: evaluate_skill
nodes.summary: MassGen evaluate entry point: type-checks the incoming RunTrace, computes run metrics and returns them as a plain dict.

nodes.name: metrics.py
nodes.summary: The metric library behind the evaluation layer — ACE, CSD, delta-ACE, delta-confidence, winner flip rate, critique-severity star and the composite TDI — all pure functions over RoundTrace/RunTrace.
nodes.languageNotes: Softmax entropy is computed with the log-sum-exp trick and variance with ddof=0, so the metrics stay numerically stable without pulling in SciPy.

nodes.name: ace
nodes.summary: Agent Confidence Entropy: the temperature-scaled softmax entropy of a round's agent confidences, the core disagreement signal.

nodes.name: ace_norm
nodes.summary: ACE normalised by log(n_agents) so rounds with different agent counts are comparable.

nodes.name: ace_d
nodes.summary: Discrete variant of ACE computed over a distribution derived from the raw confidences without temperature scaling.

nodes.name: critique_severity_dispersion
nodes.summary: Spread of critique severities within a round — how unevenly the agents criticised each other.

nodes.name: critique_severity_max
nodes.summary: The single harshest critique severity observed in a round.

nodes.name: critique_severity_star
nodes.summary: The CST statistic combining critique severity magnitude and concentration into one round-level score.

nodes.name: _flatten_critiques
nodes.summary: Flattens the N x (N-1) critique-severity matrix into a single ordered sequence, skipping the self-critique diagonal.

nodes.name: round_metrics
nodes.summary: Computes the full RoundMetrics record (ACE, normalised ACE, confidence stats, CSD, winner index, consensus score) for one RoundTrace.

nodes.name: delta_ace
nodes.summary: Change in ACE from the first to the last round — whether the agents converged or diverged in confidence.

nodes.name: delta_mean_confidence
nodes.summary: Change in mean agent confidence across the run.

nodes.name: winner_flip_rate
nodes.summary: Fraction of round transitions in which the winning agent changed — a direct instability signal.

nodes.name: tdi
nodes.summary: Task Difficulty Index: the calibrated linear combination of delta-ACE, delta-confidence, winner flip rate and severity into one scalar.

nodes.name: tdi2
nodes.summary: Second-order TDI variant adding pairwise interaction terms on top of the linear coefficients.

nodes.name: run_metrics
nodes.summary: Assembles the RunMetrics record for a whole RunTrace: per-round metrics plus the run-level deltas and TDI.

nodes.name: probe.py
nodes.summary: Preflight probe: the cheapest possible look at a task — one shallow orchestration round reduced to a four-dimensional signature the Bayesian recommender consumes.
nodes.languageNotes: Framework-agnostic by construction: it accepts a RoundTrace from a real orchestrator, a mock, or a stored log alike.

nodes.name: ProbeSignature
nodes.summary: Frozen four-dimensional task signature (normalised ACE, mean confidence, max confidence, critique dispersion) with a vector view for the recommender.

nodes.name: signature_from_round
nodes.summary: Reduces one RoundTrace to a ProbeSignature by computing normalised ACE and critique dispersion alongside the confidence statistics.

nodes.name: preflight
nodes.summary: Runs the caller-supplied shallow round, validates that it produced a trace, and returns its probe signature.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: ChipSim package root for the lung-on-chip exposure and barrier-response simulator, carrying a scaffold-integrity guard that turns an accidental PEP 420 namespace subpackage into a loud ImportError.
nodes.languageNotes: Since PEP 420 a subdirectory without __init__.py still imports as an implicit namespace package with no warning; the guard makes that silent downgrade a falsifiable failure.

nodes.name: _assert_regular_packages
nodes.summary: Walks the declared subpackages and raises ImportError if any has silently become an implicit namespace package, keeping the scaffold-integrity condition real rather than vacuous.

nodes.name: journal.py
nodes.summary: Append-only run journal: every run record carries a verified copy of every config file it used, plus environment, seed resolution and argv, so a replay cannot silently pick up today's configs and report success.
nodes.languageNotes: Configs are snapshotted by copy, never by reference, and every snapshot is digest-bound to the manifest; symlinks, hard links, FIFOs and directory links that escape the project are refused rather than skipped.

nodes.name: _recorded_argv
nodes.summary: Records argv with argv0 reduced to a basename, so a record never leaks an absolute invocation path while the argument tail is kept verbatim.

nodes.name: manifest_digest
nodes.summary: Computes the SHA-256 digest that binds a run manifest to its contents, the value every later read re-checks.

nodes.name: source_root
nodes.summary: Resolves the installed package's source root; deliberately not overridable, unlike the project root.

nodes.name: _package_versions
nodes.summary: Captures the installed versions of the pinned scientific dependencies by value, because pinned pyarrow and rdkit builds change output bytes.

nodes.name: _resolve_seed
nodes.summary: Resolves the effective random seed from the run config and environment variables, recording which source won and refusing non-integer, boolean, float or underscored values rather than recording junk.

nodes.name: _coerce_seed
nodes.summary: Coerces a candidate seed value to an int, rejecting bools, floats and underscore-separated strings that would otherwise parse misleadingly.

nodes.name: _environment
nodes.summary: Snapshots the recorded environment by value: interpreter, platform, package versions, journal relocation and the raw seed variables.

nodes.name: _validate_run_id
nodes.summary: Rejects a run id that would traverse out of the journal directory before it is ever used as a path component.

nodes.name: _config_sources
nodes.summary: Walks the configs tree and enumerates every file to snapshot, refusing escaping symlinks, symlink cycles and diamonds, hard links, FIFOs and broken links rather than silently skipping them.

nodes.name: _configs_boundary
nodes.summary: Establishes the resolved boundary the configs walk may not escape, including the case where configs itself is a link out of the tree.

nodes.name: _refuse_escaping_config
nodes.summary: Refuses any candidate config path that resolves outside the project boundary, loudly and before anything is written.

nodes.name: _open_verified_config
nodes.summary: Opens a config file only after re-verifying the path it resolved to, so the bytes snapshotted are the bytes of the path that was checked.

nodes.name: start_run
nodes.summary: Opens a run: validates the run id, snapshots every config by copy, records the environment and seed resolution, and writes the digest-bound manifest — leaving no partial directory if it fails.

nodes.name: read_manifest
nodes.summary: Reads a run manifest back, refusing a tampered manifest, one without a digest, or one whose binding check cannot be performed.

nodes.name: _verify_config_snapshot
nodes.summary: Re-hashes the snapshotted config tree against the manifest, detecting tampering, added files and relocated records.

nodes.name: outcome_digest
nodes.summary: Computes the digest binding a run outcome to its manifest so a copied outcome cannot make a crashed run read as a success.

nodes.name: finish_run
nodes.summary: Closes a run by writing the outcome last and exactly once, so a crash leaves no outcome and can never be read as success.

nodes.name: read_outcome
nodes.summary: Reads a run outcome, returning None for an unfinished run and refusing a tampered or transplanted outcome rather than reporting success.

nodes.name: record_invocation
nodes.summary: Records a one-shot invocation (rather than a full run) with its trimmed argv, never overwriting a previous invocation record.

nodes.name: JournalError
nodes.summary: Base error for journal failures such as an invalid run id or an unusable project root override.

nodes.name: ConfigIntegrityError
nodes.summary: Raised when a config snapshot fails its digest check or a config path escapes the project boundary.

nodes.name: ManifestVerificationError
nodes.summary: Raised when a manifest is tampered with, missing its digest, or does not bind to the record being read.

nodes.name: pipeline.py
nodes.summary: ETL pipeline CLI exposing the five subcommands the n8n workflow export names (fetch, hash-verify, parse, provenance-tests, write) plus the TTY-gated panel-seal command, with every invocation journalled.
nodes.languageNotes: The SUBCOMMANDS table is the single source of truth validated against the exported workflow JSON, so a renamed command fails a test rather than failing at 3am inside n8n.

nodes.name: _cmd_parse
nodes.summary: Parse subcommand: loads compounds and protein edges, adds canonical identity, and reports how many rows the canonicalization collapsed.

nodes.name: _stdin_is_interactive
nodes.summary: Reports whether stdin is a real TTY, treating a stdin object without isatty as non-interactive.

nodes.name: _read_confirmation
nodes.summary: Reads the human confirmation for an irreversible seal with a timeout, prompting on stderr so a stdout redirect cannot swallow it, and treating an interrupted or failed read as a refusal.

nodes.name: _readline_or_empty
nodes.summary: Reads one line from stdin, returning empty rather than raising when the stream is closed or unreadable.

nodes.name: _cmd_panel_seal
nodes.summary: Panel-seal subcommand: refuses without a TTY, requires a case-insensitive typed confirmation, writes nothing on refusal, and journals the attempt either way.

nodes.name: build_parser
nodes.summary: Builds the argparse parser from the SUBCOMMANDS table that the exported n8n workflow is validated against.

nodes.name: available_subcommands
nodes.summary: Returns the subcommand names the parser actually registers — the value the workflow-export test compares against.

nodes.name: _journal_best_effort
nodes.summary: Journals an action, and when the journal itself is unwritable leaves a durable UNRECORDED marker file rather than proceeding silently.

nodes.name: project_root
nodes.summary: Resolves the project root, honouring an override only when it is an existing absolute directory and raising a JournalError otherwise.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: parses argv, resolves the project root, journals the run or invocation, dispatches to the handler and normalises its exit code, recording crashes as crashes and a None return as success.

nodes.name: test_panel_seal_tty.py

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package barrel for the MassGen extractor draft, re-exporting the confidence and severity projection functions as the module's public surface.

nodes.name: confidence.py
nodes.summary: Deterministic, LLM-free projection of per-agent confidence from a round's categorical peer votes, computed as vote share with self-votes excluded and abstentions folded into the denominator.

nodes.name: AgentVoteLike
nodes.summary: Structural typing Protocol describing the minimal vote record the confidence projection needs: a voter id and the agent it voted for.
nodes.languageNotes: typing.Protocol lets the extractor accept any orchestrator vote object without importing MassGen's concrete types.

nodes.name: project_confidence
nodes.summary: Returns the per-agent projected confidence vector in agent_ids order by counting peer votes received and dividing by the number of distinct voters actually seen.

nodes.name: severity.py
nodes.summary: LLM-driven severity projection that rates each vote's free-text reason through an injected rater backend, with per-call caching and a weak default prior when the reason is missing.

nodes.name: AgentVoteLike
nodes.summary: Structural typing Protocol for a vote record carrying the voter id, its chosen target, and the free-text reason the severity rater consumes.

nodes.name: project_severity
nodes.summary: Builds the N x (N-1) critic-to-target severity matrix by rendering the prompt template per vote reason, clamping the rater's score to [0,1], and reusing cached scores for identical reasons.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the same off-diagonal column packing (col = tgt if tgt < src else tgt - 1) as perturb_eval.types.RoundTrace.

nodes.summary: Asserts that project_severity returns an N x (N-1) matrix for the given agent roster.

nodes.name: test_severity_caches_identical_reasons
nodes.summary: Verifies the rater backend is invoked only once when several votes carry the same reason text, pinning the per-call cache behaviour.

nodes.name: test_missing_reason_falls_back_to_default
nodes.summary: Checks the graceful-degradation path: an empty or missing reason skips the LLM call and yields the default severity prior.

nodes.name: DatasetSpec
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass declaring one scPerturb dataset download: remote and local filenames, resolved URL, pinned SHA256, and a minimum-byte truncation guard.

nodes.name: _fetch
nodes.summary: Core idempotent fetch: reuses a cached file when its SHA matches, discards and re-downloads it when truncated or mismatched, and raises if the fresh download still fails the size or digest check.

nodes.name: subsample.py

nodes.name: mean_abs_logfc_per_target
nodes.summary: Computes each perturbation's mean absolute log fold change on its own target gene against the control mean, yielding a faithful perturbation-strength stratifier.

nodes.name: stratified_subsample
nodes.summary: Draws at most n_per_stratum candidates from each stratum using a seeded NumPy generator and returns the sorted union, so the same seed always yields the same subset.

tour.title: Workspace Overview
tour.description: Start here to understand what bioFM actually is: not one application, but a workspace that tracks the biological foundation model landscape and turns that reading into running code. The README lays out the top-level directory contract, and CONTEXT-MAP.md names the two bounded contexts the graph covers — ChipSim and the V2R loop — along with the vocabulary they deliberately refuse to share. The key fact to carry into every later step is that the two packages under projects/ never import each other; this tour therefore walks one to completion before starting the other.

tour.title: ChipSim: Purpose and Decisions
tour.description: The first project is lung-on-chipsim, an in-silico Lung-on-a-Chip proof of concept built around a linear data spine. Its README is the entry-point guide to module responsibilities and, crucially, to what runs today versus what is still blocked, while CONTEXT.md is the ubiquitous-language document that fixes the vocabulary — data subjects, panels, roster, and the standing rules agents must obey. The three ADRs record decisions that would otherwise look like bugs: the run journal deliberately omits git state, a power floor drives a stratified roster, and the pair stratum is curated by a human rather than discovered by code.

tour.title: The Pipeline CLI and Run Journal
tour.description: pipeline.py is ChipSim's entry point: a Typer CLI exposing the five ETL subcommands (fetch, hash-verify, parse, provenance-tests, write) plus a TTY-gated panel-seal command, and every invocation is journalled. journal.py is why that matters — each append-only run record embeds a verified copy of every config file the run used, alongside environment, seed resolution and argv, so a replay can never silently pick up today's configs and still report success. The n8n workflow export is the outer driver that shells out to `python -m chipsim.pipeline`, and test_workflow_export.py keeps the two honest by asserting the exported workflow is a single connected five-node chain whose every node names a CLI entrypoint that actually exists.
tour.languageLesson: Typer builds a CLI from ordinary Python type hints — a function parameter annotated `str` becomes a required option, `Optional[str] = None` an optional one. Note also that pipeline.py imports its heavy stage modules lazily inside command bodies rather than at module top level, so `--help` stays fast and an unavailable optional dependency only breaks the one subcommand that needs it.

tour.title: Ingest and the Licensing Boundary
tour.description: The pipeline's first stage fetches, hash-verifies and parses a pinned public DrugBank 4.2 snapshot, and it deliberately takes only compound identity and drug-to-transporter edges — never affinities, and never redistributing source content. sources.yaml is the provenance register for every external source the proof of concept reads, marking each licence either verified or NEEDS_HUMAN_CONFIRMATION, while drugbank/provenance.yaml pins the source and audited commits, the CC BY-NC 4.0 licence and the explicit non-commercial commitment. The fixture README makes the same boundary concrete for tests: those TSVs only mimic the upstream schema so parse logic is testable, and carry no DrugBank content at all.
tour.languageLesson: Pinning a snapshot by commit hash plus content hash is the reproducibility idiom here: the commit says which upstream revision was intended, the hash-verify step proves the bytes on disk are that revision. Storing licence terms as structured YAML rather than prose means a test can assert on them.

tour.title: Harmonization and Panel Gating
tour.description: Once records are ingested they must be made comparable, and that is what the harmonize package does. ids.py canonicalizes compound identity through RDKit salt stripping, neutralization and tautomer canonicalization so a salt and its free base never split into two compounds; contracts.py encodes the ratified nine-key provenance contract, including the conditional rule that a change rationale is non-empty if and only if the audited commit differs from the source commit. adjudication.py merges human P-gp verdicts without ever clobbering them and keeps 'unadjudicated' distinct from 'adjudicated as unknown', while pgp_label.py joins against the barrier panel to emit a three-way substrate label — and refuses to run at all unless barrier_panel.yaml has had its `ratified: false` flag flipped by a human.
tour.languageLesson: Notice the three-valued label design: absence of an ABCB1 edge yields 'unknown', never 'no'. Modelling 'we did not observe this' separately from 'this is false' is the same discipline as distinguishing None from False in Python — collapsing them silently manufactures evidence that was never collected.

tour.title: Human Artifacts and Guards
tour.description: ChipSim's most developed subsystem is not a model — it is the set of executable guards that keep the project's commitments true, which is why these modules sit in their own verification-guards layer rather than with the ordinary tests. roster.py validates the human-written compound roster (entry count, evidence DOIs, resolvability) and pointedly never generates one, and provenance_block.py renders the model card's provenance section by composing the version string from the pinned snapshot fields from Step 4 rather than hard-coding it. test_fixtures.py, the single highest fan-in node in the whole graph, enforces that shipped source never references fixture paths and that fixture content stays locked; honesty_scan.py is a shared polarity-aware scanner for authorship-overclaim wording; test_scaffold.py turns the build plan's done-conditions into standing assertions about layout, dependency pins and config hygiene.
tour.languageLesson: These files use pytest as an assertion engine over the repository itself, not over library behaviour. A failure here is a governance breach rather than a code regression — the same runner, a completely different meaning, which is worth knowing before you 'fix' one by loosening the assertion.

tour.title: Perturb-Seq-Eval: The Thesis
tour.description: The second package is entirely independent of ChipSim and answers a different question: can you predict how hard a multi-agent task is before paying to run it? THESIS.md states the claim — agent confidence entropy as an empirical difficulty oracle, with a Bayesian pre-test for agentic hyperparameter tuning on Perturb-seq experimental design — and defines the ACE, CSD, convergence and TDI metrics you will meet in code two steps from now. DESIGN.md is the more honest read: it audits what is genuinely novel versus adapter code and names the trace schema as the project's real contract. pyproject.toml shows this is a Poetry src-layout distribution with a `perturb-eval` console script and optional dev, research, scgpt, modal and paper dependency groups.
tour.languageLesson: The src-layout (`src/perturb_eval/` rather than `perturb_eval/`) forces the package to be installed before it can be imported, which prevents tests from accidentally passing against the working directory instead of the built distribution. Poetry's optional dependency groups let a CPU-only contributor skip the GPU stack entirely.

tour.title: Core Types and Protocols
tour.description: types.py is the package's centre of gravity and its highest fan-in code node: immutable carriers for per-round and per-run orchestration traces, their derived metric records, and the Config that defines the HPO search axes. Everything downstream — metrics, optimizers, experiments, the Modal apps — speaks in these shapes, so this is the file to read slowly. __init__.py deliberately re-exports only four things (recommender, metrics, probe, trace types) as the public surface, cli.py exposes `perturb-eval preflight | calibrate | evaluate`, and data.py and model.py define the dataset and predictor Protocols that let agents depend on an interface while real scanpy and scGPT loaders stay behind optional imports.
tour.languageLesson: Two Python idioms carry this design. Frozen dataclasses (`@dataclass(frozen=True)`) give hashable, immutable value objects, so a trace cannot be mutated after the run that produced it. `typing.Protocol` gives structural typing: MockPredictor and ScGPTPredictor satisfy the same contract without inheriting from anything, which is what keeps the heavy dependency optional.

tour.title: The Metric and Recommender Stack
tour.description: This is where the thesis from Step 7 becomes arithmetic. metrics.py is a library of pure functions over the RoundTrace and RunTrace types from Step 8 — ACE, CSD, delta-ACE, winner flip rate, critique-severity star, and the composite TDI — and calibration.py fits the TDI coefficients from logged runs with a small ridge regression, turning raw orchestration signal into one difficulty index. probe.py is the cheapest possible look at a task: a single shallow orchestration round reduced to a four-dimensional signature, which bayesian.py then maps to a MAP configuration under a FLOPs budget using a per-config Gaussian likelihood and a size-favouring prior computed in log space. experiments/common.py holds the bridge that turns a full RunTrace back into a probe signature, closing the loop.
tour.languageLesson: Keeping every metric a pure function of an immutable trace means they can be recomputed from logged artifacts long after the run, which is exactly what the paper-filling step later depends on. Computing the posterior in log space is the standard numerical-stability move: products of many small probabilities underflow float64, sums of log-probabilities do not.

tour.title: Backbones and Optimizers
tour.description: Two parallel plugin stacks sit under the evaluation layer, and both follow the same shape: a base module defining a Protocol, and an __init__ acting as a name-to-class registry. backbones/base.py fixes the BackbonePredictor contract plus the pure NumPy helpers (MSD, per-perturbation mean, log fold-change) every experiment runner needs, and backbones/__init__.py maps the names linear, mlp and scgpt_small to implementations. optimizers/base.py adds the Observation carrier and the embedding that relaxes a discrete Config into a continuous vector, which is what makes numeric search possible at all: contextual_gp.py is the supplement's primary methodological contribution, a contextual GP bandit with a factored Matern-5/2 times Hamming kernel and an exact posterior, while cma_es.py is a dependency-free evolution strategy adapting step size by Rechenberg's one-fifth rule.
tour.languageLesson: The registry-in-__init__ pattern (a plain dict from string name to class) is how both stacks stay configuration-driven: a YAML file names 'contextual_gp' and the loop resolves it, with no import of the concrete class at the call site. Implementing the kernels in pure NumPy rather than reaching for GPyTorch keeps the research claim auditable and the CPU dry-run possible.

tour.title: The Agentic Lifecycle Loop
tour.description: loop.py is the highest fan-out module in the package and the thing the thesis is actually measuring: a multi-round propose, execute, critique, refine driver that threads the Validator's rationale and the previous round's MSD into the next round's context, stopping early once the Validator accepts. Its own types.py holds frozen DTOs for one executed agent step, one validation verdict and the full run record — a deliberately narrower vocabulary than the package-level traces from Step 8. architect_dispatch.py translates an Architect agent's free-form proposed configuration into a concrete backbone from Step 10 plus a normalised training config, applying the round's critique delta, and validator_gate.py scores the trained backbone on held-out perturbations and emits the structured critique that feeds the next round. openrouter_client.py is what makes running this affordable: model rotation, per-model cooldowns on rate limits, and a sha256 disk cache that makes reruns cheap and resumable.
tour.languageLesson: Content-addressed caching — hashing the request payload to a sha256 key and storing the response on disk — turns a non-deterministic paid API into a replayable pure function for any prompt seen before. It is the single most useful pattern for keeping LLM-driven research reproducible without pinning a model version you do not control.

tour.title: Experiment Runners and Real Data
tour.description: With the library in place, the experiment modules compose it into the runs the paper reports. adamson_loader.py reads the real Adamson 2016 Perturb-seq h5ad using only h5py, extracting perturbation labels and QC metrics into the package's split shape, and e2_adamson.py normalises and log1p-transforms counts, applies a leave-one-perturbation-out split and scores held-out MSD on top-K differentially expressed genes. e3_optimizer_comparison.py replays each optimizer from Step 10 against an already-filled grid for a fixed budget, which is what makes the optimizer comparison cheap and fair. configs/live.yaml is the single source of truth for a real, non-synthetic run — provider and model settings, token caps, dataset and control tokens, metric coefficients and recommender priors — and full_local_dry_run.py reproduces every supplement artifact on CPU in under five minutes with no Modal account required.
tour.languageLesson: Reading .h5ad with raw h5py rather than anndata is a deliberate dependency trade: the file format is stable enough to address directly, and dropping scanpy from the critical path is what lets the dry run start in seconds. Replaying optimizers against a pre-filled grid decouples search cost from training cost, so a comparison that would take GPU-days becomes seconds.

tour.title: Remote Execution on Modal
tour.description: Nothing in the graph's import edges will tell you this, but scripts/modal/ is where the real work runs — the Modal idiom puts imports inside function bodies so they resolve in the remote container, which the resolver cannot see. app_v05.py is the headline single-stage A100 sweep with a hard cost cap: it fetches real Adamson and Norman data, runs the trainer grid across backbones and seeds with atomic JSONL appends, then the OpenRouter-driven lifecycle sweep from Step 11. app_lifecycle.py runs the end-to-end lifecycle across seeds on the Adamson pilot, and app_biofm.py warms a persistent HuggingFace cache for BioGPT and Geneformer before rating round-0 traces into probe signatures. MODAL.md is the operator guide covering deploy, retrieval, wall time, cost and failure modes, and LIVE_RUN.md walks the secrets-and-dataset setup that must happen first.
tour.languageLesson: Modal apps are defined with decorators (`@app.function(gpu=..., timeout=..., volumes=...)`) that describe the remote container declaratively; the decorated function body executes there, not locally, which is why heavy imports belong inside it. Persistent Volumes give cross-run caches for model weights, and appending results as JSONL rather than rewriting a JSON array makes a sweep resumable after a preemption.

tour.title: Results, Manuscript and the Guard
tour.description: The tour ends where the pipeline does: committed evidence. render_figures_png.py turns the Modal result JSONs from Step 13 into the five supplement figures, and fill_v050_numbers.py substitutes {{PLACEHOLDER}} tokens in the LaTeX results section with numbers pulled from the v0.5.0 summary, so no figure in paper.tex is hand-typed. The v0.5.0 provenance record pins what that release actually cost — 3,460 seconds wall clock, 11,014 GPU-seconds, $4.04 against a $28 cap — and test_no_synthetic_generators.py is the capstone guard: a repository-wide test that fails if a synthetic Perturb-seq generator reappears anywhere, or if the manuscript re-asserts a headline claim that was retracted. Like ChipSim's guards in Step 6, it treats an honesty regression as a test failure.
tour.languageLesson: Generating the results section from a machine-written summary.json instead of transcribing numbers is the LaTeX equivalent of a build step: the manuscript becomes a compiled artifact of the run, and a stale number becomes a broken build rather than a silent error no reviewer can catch.
